Power generation NDT training for Texas City: the direct answer

Power generation NDT training for Texas City employers is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III instruction in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, aimed at boilers, heat recovery steam generators, high-energy piping and condensers. It is delivered live online and onsite at your facility under ASNT Level III oversight, and your written practice governs certification. Atlantis has no Texas City classroom. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

The summary above this section describes Texas City's power and steam base and the plant requirements that flow down to NDT contractors. This section looks at the power and steam side of that same industrial complex: cogeneration plants, refinery boilers and utility-scale generation in the region. It covers the methods and codes that apply to pressure parts in power service, how outage seasons in the Texas grid shape training, what the Texas radiography and boiler rules mean for technicians, and how SNT-TC-1A training fits alongside the other schemes that power employers sometimes ask for.

Power generation NDT work in Texas City and the upper Texas coast

In Texas City, power generation and refining are physically intertwined. The refineries and chemical plants need large volumes of steam and electricity, and much of it is produced on or next to their sites. That makes power-plant inspection skills directly marketable in a refining town.

  • Texas City cogeneration plant. A natural gas-fired cogeneration plant of about 457 MW that entered service in 1987, configured as a combined cycle with three gas turbines, supplying steam to an adjacent chemical facility and power to the Texas market. It was built and run by Calpine, which became a subsidiary of Constellation Energy in January 2026.
  • Refinery and chemical-plant steam systems. Package boilers, utility boilers, waste-heat boilers and cogeneration units inside the Texas City refineries and chemical sites. These are pressure equipment in power-type service, inspected during refinery turnarounds and boiler outages.
  • Regional generation. The upper Texas coast has large gas-fired and combined-cycle plants, including NRG's Cedar Bayou station in Baytown and the W.A. Parish plant in Fort Bend County, and the South Texas Project nuclear plant in Matagorda County. Contractors based around Texas City and Galveston County often work across all of these.

The power-generation inspection workload follows the outage calendar. In the ERCOT market, operators try to keep units available for the summer peak, so major maintenance outages concentrate in the spring and autumn shoulder seasons. Those are also the windows when Gulf Coast refineries schedule turnarounds, which means the same pool of certified technicians is in demand twice over. Employers that certify and upgrade technicians in the months before the shoulder seasons are the ones that can staff both.

Methods mapped to power and steam equipment in Texas City

MethodPower generation application in Texas CityCode or standard usually in play
UT thicknessFlow-accelerated corrosion monitoring in HRSG low-pressure sections, economisers and feedwater piping; boiler tube wall-loss surveysOwner FAC programmes; ASME Section V Article 23 (SE-797); EPRI guidance as context
PAUTExamination of high-energy piping welds, header welds and tube-to-header connections; weld repair acceptanceASME B31.1; ASME Section I; ASME Section V Article 4
TOFDThick-section main steam and hot reheat piping welds, header girth welds, often combined with PAUTASME Section V Article 4; owner specifications
RTBoiler and HRSG tube butt welds during repairs; small-bore piping welds; new constructionASME Section I; ASME B31.1; ASME Section V Article 2
MTThermal fatigue and creep-related cracking at attemperators, header ligaments, drum nozzles and supportsASME Section V Article 7
PTStainless and non-magnetic components, valve internals, alloy weldsASME Section V Article 6
VTBoiler and HRSG internal walkdowns, gas turbine borescope inspection (to OEM procedures), support and hanger inspectionsASME Section V Article 9; OEM and owner procedures
ETCondenser, feedwater heater and heat exchanger tube testing during outagesASME Section V Article 8; owner procedures

Method spotlight: UT for flow-accelerated corrosion in HRSGs. Combined-cycle and cogeneration plants like those around Texas City run heat recovery steam generators with carbon-steel low-pressure circuits that are vulnerable to flow-accelerated corrosion. FAC thins tubes and piping, especially at bends, tees and downstream of control valves, and can lead to sudden failures. Owners manage it with UT thickness programmes: grid layouts, repeat readings at the same locations, and trend analysis. A technician who understands grid layout, couplant and temperature effects, and how to record readings so they can be compared outage to outage, adds direct value to an owner's FAC programme. UT Level II with a strong thickness module is the most useful starting qualification for power work here.

High-energy piping and creep-strength-enhanced steels. Main steam and hot reheat lines in modern plants often use creep-strength-enhanced ferritic steels such as Grade 91, whose welds are prone to specific damage mechanisms if heat treatment was wrong or service conditions are harsh. PAUT and TOFD are used to examine these welds, supported by other techniques the owner specifies. SNT-TC-1A training in PAUT and TOFD builds the method skills; the owner's procedures and acceptance criteria govern each examination.

Which certification scheme Texas City power employers expect

For fossil-fuel and cogeneration plants, NDT contractors normally certify personnel to ASNT SNT-TC-1A through a written practice, and the plant owner adds its own contractor qualification. Nuclear is different. Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only; the other schemes below are context for what employers in the region also ask for.

ASME Section XI and EPRI PDI qualificationNuclear plants such as the South Texas Project, for in-service UTNo. PDI is a separate performance demonstration; SNT-TC-1A UT training is foundation only

National Board R stamp and NBIC repair requirementsRepair organisations working on boilers and pressure vesselsNo. These govern the repair organisation, not the NDT technician's certification

For the national view of nuclear requirements see nuclear NDT training; for the SNT-TC-1A model see the SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide.

The SNT-TC-1A path for Texas City power technicians, step by step

  1. Written practice. The employer's SNT-TC-1A written practice, approved by its responsible Level III, sets methods, levels, hours, exams and vision rules.
  2. Classroom training in the method and level, including the power codes (ASME Section I and B31.1) and the owner's procedures. Delivered live online for Texas City cohorts where the written practice allows.
  3. Documented experience under qualified supervision. The training requirements matrix lists SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums; employers may require more.
  4. General, specific and practical exams under a Level III. The practical uses real specimens: tube samples, piping welds, thickness blocks.
  5. Vision test, usually annual.
  6. Employer certification to the written practice.
  7. Outage-driven currency. Recertification and vision dates checked against the spring and autumn outage windows so nobody's records lapse during an outage.

For the Level II working grade see the Level II training path.

Texas radiography rules and boiler inspection context

Texas is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources or X-ray equipment is regulated by the Texas Department of State Health Services Radiation Control program under 25 TAC §289.255. Radiography companies need a DSHS licence or registration; individuals acting as radiographers need a DSHS industrial radiographer certification, which includes a 40-hour radiation safety course meeting the rule's requirements; and trainees work under the personal supervision of a radiographer trainer holding a DSHS trainer card. Confirm current requirements with DSHS and your radiation safety officer.

The DSHS credential is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification. Radiographers shooting tube welds during a Texas City boiler outage need both. Atlantis teaches RT technique and interpretation under SNT-TC-1A; it does not issue DSHS certifications.

Boilers in Texas are also subject to the state boiler programme administered by the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation, with inspections by authorised inspectors and repairs carried out to the National Board Inspection Code by appropriately accredited repair organisations. NDT technicians support those repairs and inspections; their certification still comes from their employer's written practice. For plants with marine docks in the Port of Texas City, TWIC may be required for unescorted access to MTSA-regulated areas, and plant safety orientation and drug and alcohol testing apply at every site.

Online, live-virtual or onsite: how training reaches Texas City

Atlantis does not operate a training centre in Texas City, Galveston County or the Houston area. Training reaches Texas City employers in three ways:

  • Live online theory, instructor-led and scheduled around shift and outage rotations. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite practicals at your facility, run by a Level III using your instruments and specimens that reflect power work: boiler tube sections, HRSG tube samples with wall loss, piping welds with known flaws, condenser tube standards.
  • Blended pre-outage cohorts: theory in the quieter months, onsite practicals and exams just before the spring or autumn outage window.

Employer cohorts are the normal model; individuals still need a sponsoring employer's written practice to become certified. See corporate NDT training.

Level III services and written practices for Texas City power contractors

Contractors moving from refinery work into power work, or the other way round, often find their written practice and procedures do not cover the new scope: no FAC thickness procedure, no B31.1 references, no ET procedure for condenser tubes. Atlantis supports them with:

  • Written practice development and review for SNT-TC-1A programmes covering both refinery and power scopes.
  • Outside Level III services: exam administration, procedure approval and personnel qualification. See the Texas City NDT consulting page and energy and utilities NDT consulting.
  • Procedure writing for UT thickness and FAC, PAUT and TOFD on high-energy piping, RT of tube welds, MT, PT, VT and ET.
  • Pre-outage record reviews against the owner's contractor requirements.

Book a Level III consultation for your Texas City company.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT simulator lets trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 3D environments from a laptop. Texas City trainees can rehearse UT set-ups, scan patterns and indication recognition before onsite sessions. It is practice only: it does not replace hands-on training on real specimens or the practical exam your Level III administers. See the Practical NDT page for Texas City and the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Training and Level III oversight are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Texas City cohorts are taught online and at the employer's facility under his oversight.

Frequently asked questions about power generation NDT training in Texas City

Where can I get power generation NDT training in Texas City?

Atlantis delivers power generation NDT training for Texas City employers live online and onsite at their facilities; it has no Texas City classroom. Classroom schools operate in Webster and across the Houston area.

How do I get NDT certified to work in power plants in Texas?

Be employed or sponsored by a company with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete classroom training and documented experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, pass a vision test, and the employer certifies you. Nuclear plants add further requirements.

Can I take NDT training online in Texas?

The classroom hours, yes, where the written practice accepts them. Practical training and the practical exam must be hands-on.

Which NDT method is most useful for power plant work?

UT, especially thickness work for flow-accelerated corrosion and boiler tube surveys, followed by PAUT and TOFD for high-energy piping, ET for condenser and feedwater heater tubes, and RT for tube weld repairs.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom and experience hours; see the training requirements matrix. Experience hours usually take longest.

Do I need a licence for radiography in Texas?

Yes. Companies need a DSHS licence or registration, and individual radiographers need a DSHS industrial radiographer certification under 25 TAC §289.255, separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification.

Does SNT-TC-1A training qualify me for nuclear plant UT work?

It is the foundation, not the full qualification. Nuclear in-service UT typically requires EPRI PDI performance demonstration and the utility's CP-189-based programme. Atlantis does not provide PDI qualification.

What does power generation NDT training cost in Texas City?

Quote on request. Cost depends on methods and levels, headcount, onsite versus online delivery, and whether written practice or Level III services are included. Quotes come back within one business day.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA for NDT training?

Generally only at VA-approved schools or courses on the Texas eligible training provider list. Atlantis does not claim either approval, so training with Atlantis is usually employer-paid. Check approval directly with any school you consider.

Can refinery NDT technicians move into power plant work?

Yes, and in Texas City many already work both. The methods are the same; the differences are the codes (ASME Section I and B31.1), the damage mechanisms (FAC, thermal fatigue, creep) and the owner's procedures, which training can cover.

Can you train our crew at our Texas City facility before an outage?

Yes. Theory runs online beforehand, then practicals and exams run onsite. Ask about onsite training for your Texas City crew.
